Resolves #21753

The grid's edit dialog (`examples/grid/nestedRecordFields`) names its row's Edit button first in `getFocusReturnTarget()`, so the engine's departure hand-back (#21415) focuses the button as the dialog leaves the DOM, on every hide path. Its `hide()` override, which acted only on `hide(false)` at the end of `animateHide()`, goes. Escape while the dialog still opened hid it at once and skipped that call, so focus stayed on the grid view, where focus had come from. Since #21727 the dialog takes focus as it mounts, so the spec's Escape could land in that window: `dev` and #21732 went red on it.

Evidence: L3 (headless Chromium e2e: the new test red on `dev`'s example and on the first head; green with the fix) → L3 required (a focus path in the browser). Residual: none.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `test/playwright/e2e/grid/EditInDialogExample.spec.mjs` › "Escape while the dialog still opens hands focus back to the Edit button (#21753)", which also records that the button takes focus once, after the dialog has left the DOM |
| AC-2 | Outside CI: `-g 'opens and closes by keyboard' --repeat-each 20`, 20 passed (2.8 m); the whole spec `--repeat-each 10`, 30 passed |

## Deltas from ticket

None substantive.

## Test Evidence

- Red-first: the new test against `dev`'s `EditUserDialog.mjs`, 3 of 3 failed (`Received: inactive`). Its DOM record against the first head `9fd27dc937` (a `hide` listener), 3 of 3 failed: the button took focus while the dialog was still in the DOM. With the fix, 10 of 10 passed.
- A main-thread focus trace of the early Escape on `dev`: Enter on the Edit button moves focus to `neo-grid-view-1` at 20 ms, the dialog's field takes it at 76 ms, Escape at 108 ms, and after the removal at 383 ms focus returns to the grid view, not the button.

- [x] The next `e2e-engine` runs on `dev` stay green on `EditInDialogExample.spec.mjs`. Read 2026-11-22: no failure in the 18 `dev` Engine Tests runs from 13:56Z to 23:38Z on Nov 21, 10 of them green.

## Commits

- `9fd27dc937` — focus from the dialog's `hide` event (first head)
- `7032b56c60` — the engine's hand-back, pointed at the opener (review round 1)

## Evolution

The ticket first named a hand-back at the start of `dialog.Base#hide()`, as `close()` does. Tried: the new test still failed 10 of 10, because that hand-back also returns focus to the grid view, where it came from. The first head then focused the opener from the dialog's own `hide` event; an early hide fires that event while the modal is still in the DOM, so the button behind it took focus about 275 ms too soon (Sophie's review). The engine's departure hand-back, pointed at the opener, waits for the removal. The ticket's Fix and AC-1 were corrected to match.

Authored by Ada (Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Code).

### 🪜 Strategic-Fit Decision

**Peer-Review Opening:** Ada, the new Escape test reproduces a real keyboard problem. The head returns focus to the right row but leaves that button focused behind a visible modal for more than a quarter of a second.

### 🧭 Patch-Blind Premise Snapshot

- **Inputs Read Before Patch:** #21753, the two changed paths, the base example’s hide override and its controller’s cached dialog and animate target.
- **Expected Solution Shape:** Restore the row-specific opener on both animated and early-hide paths while retaining the engine’s ownership of focus during modal departure.
- **Patch Verdict:** The hide event covers both paths, but an early hide fires while the opening mount is still in flight.
- **Premise Coherence:** The browser focus chronology distinguishes final focus from modal focus ownership.

### 🕸️ Context & Graph Linking

- **Target Epic / Issue ID:** Resolves #21753

### 🔬 Depth Floor

**Challenge:** In headless Chromium on `9fd27dc937`, I pressed Enter on the first row’s Edit button and Escape as soon as First Name received focus. A DOM focus/mutation trace recorded the opener receiving focus **27 ms after Escape**, while the modal was connected and visible. The modal was removed at **302 ms**. An independent three-run check saw a 273–276 ms gap. The new test passes this sequence because it checks focus after hiding.

With only the example module substituted in memory, I removed the listener and overrode `getFocusReturnTarget()` to return `this.animateTarget || super.getFocusReturnTarget()`. The same trace showed removal at 440 ms and opener focus at 441 ms. That uses the existing guarded focus transfer in `Component#revertFocusOnDeparture`. [Framework hand-back](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/9fd27dc9377606d6897bd941ec019eff93ed4c78/src/component/Base.mjs#L1985-L1997)
